case.case_title: Hettiarachchi v. Mahaweli Authority of Sri Lanka and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC Application No. 131/2000, decided on 11 September 2000

clause.text: All persons are equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner's fundamental right under Article 12(1) was infringed by disciplinary action taken against him for refusing to permit use of public property for a political purpose.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner argued that his fundamental right under Article 12(1) was infringed when he was fined and transferred without a proper disciplinary inquiry after refusing to allow political activists to use the Mahaweli Authority office premises and facilities.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents contended that the petitioner failed to extend due obligation to personnel on official duty and justified the disciplinary action based on the petitioner's refusal to make a statement during the preliminary investigation.
key_facts: The petitioner was an Assistant Security Supervisor on night duty at the Mahaweli Authority office.
A group of persons, including political activists, requested permission to stay overnight and use office facilities for a political meeting.
The petitioner refused permission due to lack of instructions from superiors and absence of authority to provide accommodation.
Disciplinary proceedings were initiated based on complaints alleging misconduct related to refusal to assist persons on official duty.
The petitioner was fined and transferred without a proper disciplinary inquiry and without being informed of the nature of the misconduct alleged.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that Article 12(1) guarantees equal protection of the law and prohibits unequal treatment and political discrimination, including misuse of state resources for political purposes. The petitioner’s refusal to allow misuse of public property for political activities was protected under this clause.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found that the disciplinary proceedings were a gross abuse of power as the complaints did not allege any misconduct. The petitioner was penalized for resisting improper political influence, which constituted an infringement of his fundamental right under Article 12(1).
principles_established: Use of state or corporation resources for the benefit of one political party constitutes unequal treatment and political discrimination.
Employees have the right to resist improper political influence without fear of punishment.
Disciplinary action must comply with procedural fairness, including informing the employee of the nature of the misconduct and holding a proper inquiry.

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner's fundamental right under Article 12(1) was infringed, quashed the disciplinary orders, and awarded compensation and costs to the petitioner.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The transfer and fine orders dated 19.01.2000 and 07.02.2000 were quashed. The Mahaweli Authority was directed to pay Rs. 100,000 as compensation and the second respondent to pay Rs. 25,000 as costs.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(1) was central to the court's reasoning as it protects against unequal treatment and political discrimination, which was the core issue in penalizing the petitioner for resisting misuse of public property for political purposes.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court stated that the use of state and corporation resources for the benefit of one political party constitutes unequal treatment and political discrimination, and penalizing the petitioner for resisting such improper influence infringed his fundamental right under Article 12(1).
